newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's LUKoil to boost oil, product exports in 97.
newsitem.headline: Russia's LUKoil to boost oil, product exports in 97.

text.p: Russia's biggest oil company, LUKoil LKOH.RTS, plans to boost its exports of crude oil and oil products in 1997, according to its annual report, released on Thursday.
"In 1997, we plan to increase the volume of free-market oil exports," said the report, issued at the annual shareholders' meeting.
LUKoil's non-state mandated oil exports in 1996 were 16.5 million tonnes (330,000 barrels per day), down 10 percent from 18.4 million tonnes (368,000 bpd) in 1995.
The report said free-market exports were reduced because deliveries abroad under so-called federal programmes rose.
Moscow funds various projects through state-controlled oil exports, with the rights to export distributed among oil producers, including LUKoil, and trading companies.
LUKoil's product exports are also expected to rise in 1997.
"We want to increase exports of our oil products and to improve the quality," LUKoil President Vagit Alekperov told the meeting.
Product exports in 1997 would rise to 6.0 million tonnes, up one third from 4.5 million tonnes in 1996.
LUKoil refined 19.3 million tonnes (386,000 barrels per day) of oil last year and is looking to boost refining operations to 19.8 million tonnes (396,000 bpd) in 1997.
The company had previously announced plans to boost oil production in 1997 to around 59.7 million tonnes (1.19 million bpd) from 58.5 million (1.17 million bpd) in 1996.
The company, which says it has the largest proven oil reserves of any listed company in the world, accounts for nearly 20 percent of Russia's total oil output.
The annual report said LUKoil could produce an additional seven million tonnes of oil annually by the year 2000 due to technological improvements.
